title: Implementing HUMAN Skills Studio Framework, Phase 1
author: Doan Winkel
summary: Doan Winkel continues his series on the HUMAN Skills Studio Framework for teachers guiding college students in using generative AI to develop human skills. Phase 1 is a three-month pilot inside one course built on a single insight: grading only final products rewards whoever orchestrates AI best, so learning must be made visible through process evidence and human performance. He lays out a four-part Human Skills Lab, assessment types that force live human performance such as oral defense and role-play, and three pilot assignment patterns. He then covers lightweight evidence collection, workload guardrails such as grading by sampling, and common failure modes. It is a practical implementation guide for instructors rather than a theoretical argument.
points: If you grade only final products, you reward whoever uses AI most effectively, so assessment must include process evidence and a no-AI human performance moment.
The Human Skills Lab follows a repeatable rhythm of modeling, paired practice, human performance and reflection, grounded in deliberate practice research.
Oral defense, live explanation, facilitation, critique memos and role-play make student thinking visible and are hard to outsource to AI.
Sustainable evidence collection (pre/post self-ratings, one-minute reflections, compliance tracking) and sampling-based grading keep the pilot from consuming the instructor.
Common failure modes such as labs turning into lectures or oral defenses becoming pro forma each have a concrete fix.
quotes: if you grade only final products, you reward whoever orchestrates AI most effectively, not whoever learned the most.

expertise develops when learners work on specific sub-skills, receive immediate feedback, and practice at the edge of their current ability. Random practice makes permanent; only deliberate practice makes better.
Part 1: Instructor Modeling (5–10 minutes) You demonstrate the target skill and the AI role students will use. Don’t lecture about the skill, do the thing while narrating your thinking.
Oral defense is inherently AI-proof because it assesses the person, not just the text. Students who relied heavily on AI without understanding cannot defend positions they didn’t develop.
Students can use AI extensively to develop their argument, but they must own it when challenged. The live defense reveals whether they understand their own position.
You cannot deeply grade every artifact from every student. You don’t need to.
